blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Dense global attention is crucial for capturing cross-view geometry in visual geometry foundation models, yet its quadratic complexity limits efficient inference on long image sequences. Existing sparse attention methods primarily select entries of the global attention matrix based on attention probabilities and construct masks independently across layers, overlooking value redundancy and cross-layer information reuse. By analyzing attention distributions and clustering value representations across layers, we reveal two forms of \emph{cross-layer consistency}, characterized by highly similar attention probability distributions and localized changes in value redundancy structures. Building on these observations, we propose \textbf{DuCo}, a training-free sparse attention framework that exploits historical attention information and value redundancy for efficient geometric inference. Specifically, DuCo leverages historical attention information to estimate current-layer dense attention probabilities and introduces value clustering to exploit redundancy, with clusters efficiently refined through local updates across layers. Both factors are integrated through probability-weighted value distortion to jointly optimize four cluster representation states under an attention budget for sparse mask construction. Experiments across three visual geometry foundation models and five benchmarks demonstrate favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-offs.
blocks.zh: 敏锐的全球关注对于捕捉视觉几何地基模型中的交叉视野几何至关重要,然而其四相复杂性限制了对长图像序列的有效推断. 现有的稀有关注方法主要根据关注概率选择全球关注矩阵的条目,并跨层独立构建口罩,俯瞰价值冗余和跨层信息再利用. 通过分析各层的注意力分布和集群值表示,我们揭示出\emph{跨层一致性}两种形式,其特点是高度相近的注意力概率分布和价值冗余结构的局部变化. 基于这些观察,我们提议\textbf{DuCo},这是一个无训练的零散关注框架,利用历史关注信息和价值冗余来有效进行几何推断。 具体来说,DuCo利用历史关注信息来估计当前层次的密集关注概率,并引入了价值集群来利用冗余,集群通过分层局部更新得到高效的完善. 这两个因素都通过概率加权价值扭曲来整合,以便联合优化四个集群代表状态,在稀少的遮罩建筑的注意预算之下。 跨越3个视觉几何基础模型和5个基准的实验显示了有利的精度效率取舍.

blocks.en: Recovering 3D scene geometry from images is a fundamental problem in computer vision, providing the spatial understanding required for autonomous navigation, robotic perception, and augmented reality [ 19 , 17 , 12 ] . Recent advances in feed-forward visual geometry foundation models, such as VGGT [ 25 ] and π 3 \pi^{3} [ 29 ] , have enabled joint estimation of camera poses and dense scene geometry from uncalibrated multi-view images in a single forward pass. Central to these models is global self-attention, which integrates information across input views to capture geometric relationships. However, this mechanism densely evaluates all entries of the global attention matrix, incurring a computational cost that grows quadratically with the total token count. As the number of input views increases, the computational cost of dense attention becomes a major bottleneck to efficient geometric inference.
blocks.zh: 从图像中恢复3D场景几何是计算机视觉中的一个基本问题,提供了自主导航,机器人感知,并增强现实[19,17,12]所需的空间理解. 近代的向导视觉几何基础模型的进步,如VGGT[25]和\\ 3\pi\ 3}[29],使得相机外观和密集的场景几何能够从单向前行的未校正多视图图像中联合估计出. 这些模型的核心是全球自觉,它集成跨输入视图的信息来捕捉几何关系. 然而,这一机制对全球关注矩阵的所有条目进行了密集评价,导致计算成本与总指数成四倍增长。 随着输入视图数量的增加,密集关注的计算成本成为高效几何推断的一个主要瓶颈.

blocks.en: Existing sparse attention methods for visual geometry foundation models reduce computational costs by selecting important entries from the global attention matrix or adapting sparsity across layers and heads [ 24 , 3 , 11 ] . However, these methods primarily emphasize attention importance, without fully accounting for redundancy among the associated value representations. Since dense attention computes a probability-weighted sum of values, even high-probability entries may convey redundant information when their corresponding values are similar. Moreover, existing methods largely rely on layer-specific information for sparsification, leaving the cross-layer relationships of attention probabilities and value redundancy insufficiently exploited. These limitations motivate a joint investigation of attention probabilities and value redundancy, particularly their relationships across successive global attention layers.
blocks.zh: 视觉几何基础模型现有的稀有关注方法通过从全球关注矩阵中选择重要条目或调整跨地层和头部的溅射量来降低计算成本[24,3,11]. 然而,这些方法主要强调注意的重要性,没有充分考虑到相关价值表述之间的冗余。 由于密集的注意计算出一个概率加权的值和,即使高概率的条目也可能在相应的值相近时传递冗余信息. 此外,现有方法在很大程度上依赖分层信息来进行斯帕氏化,使得注意力概率和价值冗余的跨层关系没有得到充分利用. 这些限制促使人们联合调查注意力的概率和价值的冗余,特别是它们在全球各个关注层次之间的关系。

blocks.en: To investigate these relationships, Fig. 1 quantifies the evolution of attention probabilities and value redundancy across VGGT layers, using the top-20% entry overlap and local transition ratio of cluster assignments. The results reveal dual aspects of cross-layer consistency, where attention probability distributions remain highly similar across neighboring layers, while changes in value redundancy structures are largely localized. Visualizations of attention matrices and value clustering at Layers 3–4 and 15–16 further illustrate these observations. This consistency motivates reusing historical attention information and value clustering results as priors for subsequent layers. Building on this insight, we propose a training-free sparse attention framework that propagates and refines historical priors across global attention layers. Specifically, previously computed attention logits and current-layer regional estimates are combined to approximate dense attention probabilities by accounting for unobserved entries in softmax normalization. Cross-layer regional consistency further calibrates historical probabilities, while current regional estimates provide probabilities for previously unobserved entries. Meanwhile, historical value clusters are locally refined using current-layer value representations, avoiding repeated global clustering. Based on the estimated probabilities and refined clusters, four representation states, Drop, Rep, History, and Exact, are introduced to capture varying degrees of attention importance and value redundancy. These states are jointly selected by minimizing probability-weighted value distortion under an attention budget to construct sparse attention masks. The resulting attention information and updated value clusters are propagated to subsequent layers for efficient reuse.
blocks.zh: 为了调查这些关系,图一将VGGT各层的注意力概率和值冗余度的演化量化,采用集群任务的上-20%输入重合和本地过渡比率. 结果揭示出跨层一致性的双重方面,即注意力概率分布在相邻地层之间仍然高度相近,而价值冗余结构的变化则在很大程度上是局部的. 第3至4层和第15至16层的注意力矩阵和价值组合的可视化进一步说明了这些观察。 这种一致性激励人们将历史关注信息和价值分组结果作为随后各层的前身重新使用。 基于这一见解,我们提出了一个免费的零散关注框架,在全球关注层宣传和完善历史先例。 具体地说,以前计算过的注意记录和当前水平的区域估计,通过计算软磁态化中未观察到的条目,结合了大约密集的注意概率。 跨层次的区域一致性进一步校准了历史概率,而目前的区域估计则为以前未观察到的条目提供了概率. 同时,历史价值集群利用当前层次的价值表述方式在当地得到完善,避免了重复的全球集群. 根据估计的概率和精细的集群,引入了四个代表状态: Drop, Rep, History, and Exact, 以捕捉不同程度的注意力重要性和价值冗余. 这些状态通过在注意力预算中尽量减少概率加权价值扭曲来共同选择,以构建稀少的注意力罩. 由此产生的关注信息和更新的值组被传播到随后各层,以便高效地再利用。

blocks.en: Our contributions are summarized as follows: • We identify two forms of cross-layer consistency in global attention, characterized by similar attention probability distributions across neighboring layers and localized changes in value redundancy structures. • We develop a training-free sparse attention framework that leverages cross-layer consistency to propagate historical priors. Historical attention information guides dense attention probability estimation, while inherited value clusters are refined through local updates. Both components are further integrated into a probability-weighted value distortion objective to jointly optimize cluster representation states for sparse mask construction. • Extensive experiments across diverse visual geometry foundation models and benchmarks demonstrate that DuCo substantially improves inference efficiency while preserving competitive geometric reconstruction accuracy, achieving a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off.
blocks.zh: • 我们的贡献概述如下: 我们确定了全球关注的两种跨层次一致性形式,其特点是相邻层的注意概率分布相近,以及价值冗余结构的局部变化。 我们开发了一个免费的零星关注框架,利用跨层一致性来宣传历史往事。 历史关注信息指导了密集关注概率估计,而所继承的价值集群则通过本地更新来完善. 这两个组成部分被进一步纳入概率加权值扭曲目标,以联合优化分组代表状态,用于稀有的口罩构造。 各种可视几何基础模型和基准的广泛实验表明,DuCo在保持竞争性几何重建准确性的同时,大大提高了推论效率,实现了有利的准确性-效率取舍。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Feed-forward Visual Geometry Transformers. Traditional multi-view geometry pipelines rely on explicit feature matching and iterative optimization [ 23 , 19 , 16 ] . Feed-forward visual geometry Transformers instead infer cross-view structure directly from image tokens, spanning pairwise point-map regression [ 27 ] , joint multi-view reconstruction [ 32 , 1 ] , and unified prediction of camera poses, depth, and point maps [ 25 ] . Compared with pairwise reconstruction, joint multi-view formulations aggregate geometric information from multiple observations within a single forward pass, reducing the need for separate cross-view alignment. This places greater emphasis on effective feature exchange across views, particularly as the number of input images increases. These models differ in how geometric information is represented and exchanged. VGGT [ 25 ] combines frame-wise and global attention, while π 3 \pi^{3} [ 29 ] employs a permutation-equivariant formulation and VGGT- Ω \Omega [ 26 ] adopts register-based scene aggregation. Other advances explore depth-ray representations [ 15 ] and extend geometric inference to heterogeneous inputs [ 10 , 9 ] , streaming observations [ 34 , 38 ] , and dynamic scenes [ 37 , 5 , 36 ] . Despite these advances, global attention remains essential for cross-view information exchange in many architectures, while its quadratic complexity increasingly limits long-sequence inference.

blocks.en:
Efficient Inference for Visual Geometry Transformers. Efficient inference for visual geometry Transformers has been explored through token reduction [ 20 , 2 , 28 , 33 , 22 ] , compact scene representations [ 4 , 8 , 31 ] , and sparse attention [ 3 , 24 ] . FastVGGT [ 20 ] prunes redundant tokens, while FlashVGGT [ 30 ] compresses global context into descriptor tokens. In contrast, sparse attention reduces the number of evaluated entries in the global attention matrix while retaining the original token sequence. Block-Sparse Global Attention [ 24 ] selects salient blocks using pooled query and key features, while SAF3R [ 3 ] combines head-wise profiling with online adaptation. HeSS [ 11 ] reallocates sparsity according to head sensitivity, whereas Speed3R [ 18 ] learns coarse-to-fine sparse selection. AVGGT [ 21 ] instead simplifies early global layers and subsamples keys and values. Despite their different strategies, these methods primarily rely on layer-specific attention importance or sparsity characteristics, often prioritizing high-probability entries to preserve dense attention outputs.
In the broader context of model adaptation, PhaseLoRA [ 6 ] explores control-regime-conditioned low-rank adaptation for continuous-action vision-language-action policies. Beyond geometric models, prior studies have theoretically examined the benefits of considering value representations in attention approximation [ 7 ] , while others directly reuse important token selections [ 35 ] or attention weights [ 14 ] across layers. These approaches explore value-aware approximation and historical information reuse, but do not jointly exploit their cross-layer relationships for sparsification. In contrast, DuCo leverages dual cross-layer consistency in attention probabilities and value redundancy, adapting historical information and integrating both factors through a unified probability-weighted distortion objective.

blocks.zh: 3.1 全球注意力的一致性

blocks.en: Fig. 1 illustrates the cross-layer relationships of attention probabilities and value redundancy in VGGT. These visualizations reveal pronounced dual cross-layer consistency in attention probability distributions and value redundancy structures. Specifically, attention distributions remain highly similar across neighboring layers, with high-probability entries for the same query largely preserved, as exemplified by Layers 15 and 16 in Fig. 1 (a). This consistency may reflect the shared underlying scene geometry, which encourages attention to emphasize similar geometric correspondences despite evolving token representations. Such consistency suggests that historical attention information can guide the identification of important entries in subsequent layers, reducing redundant computations. To characterize value redundancy, we perform value clustering across layers, as shown in Fig. 1 (b). Although cluster assignments evolve with network depth, their changes remain largely localized, with an average local transition ratio of 70.78% across consecutive global attention layers of VGGT on 7Scenes. This localized variation suggests relatively stable value redundancy structures, allowing historical clustering results to be efficiently refined rather than recomputed globally at each layer. Collectively, these observations motivate propagating historical priors across layers to support attention probability estimation and value redundancy modeling.

blocks.en: 3.2 Propagation of Historical Priors
blocks.zh: 3.2 宣传历史往事

blocks.en: The cross-layer consistency observed in Sec. 3.1 suggests that previously computed attention information and value clustering results can serve as historical priors for subsequent layers. However, directly reusing these priors presents two challenges. First, sparse attention probabilities differ from their dense counterparts due to the exclusion of unobserved entries from softmax normalization, while variations in attention distributions across layers further limit the reliability of historical probabilities. Second, although value redundancy structures remain largely consistent, changes in value representations may lead to variations in cluster assignments, making direct reuse of historical clustering results inaccurate. To address these challenges, we develop two complementary approaches: history-guided attention probability estimation , which accounts for unobserved entries and calibrates historical probabilities according to cross-layer variations, and local refinement of value clusters , which updates inherited clustering results using current-layer value representations. Together, these approaches enable efficient propagation and adaptation of historical priors for subsequent attention sparsification.

blocks.en: With the estimated dense attention probabilities p ^ i ​ j ( ℓ ) \hat{p}_{ij}^{(\ell)} and refined value clusters 𝒫 ( ℓ ) = { C 1 , … , C K } \mathcal{P}^{(\ell)}=\{C_{1},\ldots,C_{K}\} , we construct sparse attention masks by jointly considering entry importance and value redundancy. While attention probabilities indicate the importance of individual entries, value redundancy determines whether their contributions can be approximated by shared representations. Accordingly, we adopt value clusters as the basic units for sparsification and introduce four representation states: Drop , Representative (Rep) , History , and Exact . Drop discards all entries in a cluster, while Rep retains only its representative to approximate the remaining members. History preserves previously evaluated entries together with the representative, whereas Exact retains all entries without approximation. These states provide different trade-offs between representation fidelity and computational cost.

blocks.en: 4.1 Implementation Details
blocks.zh: 4.1 详细执行情况

blocks.en: Experiments use three visual geometry foundation models, VGGT [ 25 ] , π 3 \pi^{3} [ 29 ] , and VGGT- Ω \Omega [ 26 ] , with camera pose estimation and point-cloud reconstruction evaluated on ScanNet, 7Scenes, ETH3D, NRGBD, and DTU. Following FastVGGT [ 20 ] and SAF3R [ 3 ] , 50 ScanNet test sequences form densely sampled 100-, 300-, 500-, and 1000-frame inputs, while other datasets use sparsely sampled inputs of up to 128 frames. AVGGT [ 21 ] is reproduced with a K/V subsampling factor of 4, while SAF3R uses the DINO Top-16 configuration. Camera pose estimation is evaluated using AUC, and point-cloud reconstruction using Accuracy (Acc), Completeness (Comp), and Chamfer Distance (CD), as applicable. Inference efficiency is measured by inference latency (s), acceleration ratio (Spd.) relative to the dense backbone, and allocated GPU memory (Mem.). DuCo is implemented as a training-free module that sparsifies only global attention, without modifying model parameters. The entry sparsity across all global attention layers is set to 90%, corresponding to a 10% retention ratio. For probability estimation, regions contain 256 keys, with consistency coefficient τ = 0.5 \tau=0.5 . The number of value clusters is set to 10% of the patch token count. All experiments are conducted on a single NVIDIA H800 GPU.

Under the same nominal budgets, replacing regional with historical probability estimation improves AUC@3 from 11.18 to 17.44 and reduces CD from 0.158 to 0.152, demonstrating the benefit of historical information for entry selection. By introducing value clustering and Drop/Rep/Exact states, variant (c) further improves AUC@3 to 19.76 and CD to 0.139 relative to variant (a), highlighting the importance of value-aware approximation. blocks.en: 4.5 Efficiency Analysis
blocks.zh: 4.5 效率分析

blocks.en: Figure 3(a) compares the inference time breakdown across different methods. As the sequence length increases, global attention becomes the dominant computational bottleneck. DuCo achieves 2.94 × \times and 4.53 × \times speedups over dense VGGT with 100 and 500 frames, respectively. Unlike layer-independent sparsification methods, DuCo reduces overhead by reusing previously computed information. Specifically, historical probability estimates are derived during preceding sparse attention computations, while local clustering and query grouping reduce redundant operations. Moreover, although attention probabilities vary across queries, the value-distortion terms are query-independent and can be precomputed and shared across queries and cluster representation states, avoiding repeated value comparisons. These designs keep overhead limited relative to the savings in attention computation. Nevertheless, as shown in Figure 3(b) , the proportion of overhead attributed to state optimization increases with sequence length, reflecting the growing number of cluster-state decisions.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We present DuCo, a training-free sparse attention framework motivated by dual cross-layer consistency in global attention. Similarity in attention probability distributions and localized changes in value redundancy suggest that preceding-layer information can guide sparsification. DuCo estimates current-layer dense attention probabilities by compensating for unobserved entries in historical sparse computations and adapting historical importance to regional distribution shifts. Value clustering captures redundancy, while local refinement updates inherited clusters as features evolve. The estimated probabilities and refined clusters are coupled through probability-weighted value distortion, which guides the selection of four representation states under an attention budget. Experiments on three visual geometry foundation models and five benchmarks confirm that this treatment improves inference efficiency while maintaining competitive geometric accuracy.
blocks.zh: 我们提出DuCo,这是一个无训练的零散关注框架,其动机是全球关注的双层一致性。 关注概率分布的相似性和值冗余的局部变化表明,前层信息可以指导斯波化. DuCo通过补偿历史稀有计算中未观察到的条目并调整历史重要性以适应区域分布变化,来估计当前层次的密集关注概率. 价值集群捕捉冗余,而本地精细更新则随着特性的演化而继承了集群. 估计概率和精细的组别通过概率加权价值扭曲相配合,从而指导在注意预算下选择四个代表国。 对3个可视几何基础模型和5个基准的实验证实,这种处理在保持有竞争力的几何精度的同时提高了推论效率.
